title: Pre-shipment inspection: how buyers check quality before goods leave
summary: An inspection before shipment helps confirm that goods match the agreed specification, quantity and packing. Clear written specifications make it work.

title: Jute as a natural fibre material: a buyer's guide
summary: Jute is a plant-based fibre used for sacks, bags, cloth and yarn. This guide covers its properties, its limits and what to specify when you buy.

title: International payment terms: advance, letter of credit, collection and open account
summary: How you get paid shapes the risk for both sides. The four common methods sit on a spectrum from most secure for the seller to most secure for the buyer.

title: Incoterms 2020 explained for importers and exporters
summary: Incoterms are eleven three-letter rules published by the International Chamber of Commerce. They set out who arranges transport, insurance and customs clearance, and where risk passes from seller to buyer.

title: Importing food into the EU, UK and USA: first steps
summary: A starting checklist for each of three major markets. Rules depend on the exact product, so use this to know what to ask, then confirm with the official authority or a licensed customs broker.

title: How to track commodity prices, and what usually moves them
summary: Prices of agricultural and other commodities move for reasons you can watch: harvests, energy and freight, currencies and policy. This guide shows where to follow them and how to protect a contract.

title: How to research an export market with free trade data
summary: A short, repeatable method to see who buys a product, how much, from whom and under what conditions, using public trade statistics and tariff databases.

title: HS codes explained: why classification decides your duty and paperwork
summary: The Harmonized System is the international product code used by customs worldwide. The code you declare affects the duty rate, import rules and statistics for your shipment.

title: Export documents checklist: what a typical shipment needs
summary: A shipment usually travels with a core set of documents, plus extra certificates for food, plants and animal products. Mismatched details are a common cause of delay.

title: Certificates of origin and trade agreements in plain language
summary: A certificate of origin states where goods were made. When a trade agreement applies, proof of origin can lead to lower or zero import duty.
